parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile federal layer with a protective state judiciary. Traveller-facing exposures are tier-1 and universal: passport/visa markers fixed to birth sex with X markers barred, documented confiscation stranding travellers, cable instructions to refuse 'sex doubt' cases and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility, federal exclusion from government-funded single-sex facilities, birth-sex custody placement (a trans woman held 24h in a men's ward), documented immigration-detention abuse, and federal conversion-therapy-style prison policy. Multiple foreign governments issued travel advisories. Offsetting: no criminalisation of trans identity, national hate-crime and employment protections, and state courts repeatedly enjoining every restrictive state law — the only state improving in the July 2026 assessment. Net: documented universal exposures with partial, working recourse.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal order fixes sex at birth on passports/visas; X markers barred for new issues; foreign ministry stopped processing mismatched markers Feb 2025, upheld by Supreme Court Nov 2025. travellers report passports confiscated or blocked, stranded abroad. Cable instructs refusal where documents cast 'reasonable doubt' on sex, and consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility. Eight-plus governments issued travel advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, limited waivers, never automatic; ACLU suit pending in national courts; legal-aid FAQ on document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal → possible fraud allegation → immigration custody, where documented trans abuse (beatings, solitary, sexual abuse of trans men) sits downstream. State courts cannot reach federal document or entry rules.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policy for trans inmates (hair cutting, hormone removal) from 2026; trans prisoner counts no longer reported. Immigration custody: forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse of trans trans men. State: trans woman arrested under bathroom law held 24 hours in the men's ward. Federal prison-policy EO protections rescinded.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; state courts apply equal-protection/dignity guarantees; arrest was prosecuted as trespass only (60-day misdemeanour), not identity crime.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can cascade into custody where birth-sex placement applies; state constitutional protections do not reach federal prisons or immigration detention.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity (universal exposure). State facilities bill (Feb 2025) on publicly funded venues enjoined April 2025 — status since uncertain. Nationally 21+ units restrict facilities, 4 criminalise in certain circumstances; one arrest under such a law (Mar 2025).
federal_state_facilities.protection: State district judge found the facilities law motivated by animus with no safety evidence and restrained it; state house defeated a narrower ban Dec 2024; 2018 ballot initiative failed.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Even if the state ban stays enjoined, federal facility exclusion for federally funded buildings operates regardless of state law.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders and funding moves hostile to gender-affirming care; October 2025 proposed rule barring public insurance reimbursement for under-18 care; DOJ subpoenaed hospital records of under-19 patients (summer 2025); LGBTQ youth services removed from national crisis lifeline. For a travelling minor, federal hostility is operative.
care_services.protection: State care ban permanently struck down 14 May 2025; state highest court kept injunction and suggested trans status as suspect class; adult care not prohibited in state.
care_services.interaction: State permission does not restore federally funded services or shield records from federal subpoenas; a visiting family's care-seeking can expose them to federal data collection.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; December 2025 reward memo frames 'radical gender ideology' among violent-extremist viewpoints; EOs describe care as 'mutilation' and direct investigation of 'gender ideology' in schools. 2025 poll: 66% back birth-sex document rules. State flag law bans Pride flags; drag events restricted.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The reward criterion never lists gender ideology; strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; a bill defining drag as inherently sexual was defeated; drag-hour order is restrained as overbroad.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises outing probability and chilling effects even where statutes are enjoined; state house pushes back at the legislative level.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal EO calls minors' care 'mutilation' and directs criminal investigation of teachers facilitating social transition; federal facility bans reach K-12 schools; proposed insurance bar for under-18 care. A visiting trans minor faces birth-sex facility rules in federally funded schools/buildings and heightened scrutiny at entry.
minors_guardians.protection: State permits gender-affirming care for minors (ban struck down); state constitution's equal-protection record shields minors' care locally; parental rights (adoption, opt-in sex ed) unimpaired.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor moves between a protective state care regime and hostile federal funding, record-subpoena and facility rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific incidents, counts or rates documented — unknown, not safe. National record: bias against sexual orientation is one-seventh to one-fifth of single-bias hate incidents; only 23 units cover gender identity in bias-crime statutes; state hate-crime law omits gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity and applies in the state; employment discrimination prohibited nationally since 2020; municipal public-accommodation ordinances; state courts demonstrably protective.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence in the state would be prosecuted federally, but state-level omission thins the first response layer.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unknowns: whether the April 2025 facilities TRO became permanent or the law took effect; outcome of the April 2026 challenge to the 2026 biological-definitions bill (which would rewrite licences and anti-discrimination law); status of the marker-change block beyond the April 2026 affirmance; several federal orders blocked or enjoined, so exposure shifts by travel date. Religious 'licence to discriminate' law (2021) operative.
remedies_unknowns.protection: State courts have blocked or enjoined every major anti-trans statute (2023 bill, 2022 rules, care ban, sports ban, facilities bill); state was the sole improved entry in the July 2026 national assessment; ACLU litigation, legal-aid FAQ, national employment and hate-crime recourse function.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: State remedies work for trans people but cannot override federal entry, document, facility-funding or custody rules — the operative interactions remain federal.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's universal entry exclusion with no remedy resembles this dossier's federal document/refusal regime and foreign travel advisories. This rates higher: no arrest or criminal charge follows discovery, the fraud bar is expressly non-automatic with waivers and pending litigation, and state courts demonstrably grant relief — Vellandra's appeals are near-worthless.

Kestrel Isles' discretionary secondary screening, refusal and slow appeals captures the entry axis. This rates lower because exposures extend beyond the border into federal facility exclusion, birth-sex custody placement with documented harm (men's ward, conversion-therapy-style prison policy, immigration-detention abuse) and a lifetime fraud finding — a broader and more severe stack than administrative refusal.

Drellia's mandatory registration, nightly hotel transmission and database-driven exposure with an ineffective ombuds resembles the continuous federal document exposure here. Similar tier, but this dossier adds documented custodial abuse and state-issued advisories (worse), while Drellia lacks any working remedy and this state's courts repeatedly strike hostile laws (better) — netting slightly below 0.45.

Meridia's trained border staff, tribunal appeals and brief detention is well above this case. Federal policy here actively targets trans documents, X markers and facilities, and custody harm is documented; only the state-level judiciary approaches Meridia's remedial quality, and it cannot reach the border or federal custody.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets two regimes at once. The federal layer supplies the heaviest, unavoidable exposures: birth-sex-locked documents with X markers barred and reports of passports seized, entry-officer instructions to refuse on sex doubt and weigh a lifetime fraud bar, exclusion from federally funded single-sex facilities, birth-sex custody placement, and documented abuse in immigration detention — enough foreign states to issue advisories to warrant them. The state layer genuinely mitigates: its courts have enjoined every enacted restriction, care remains legal, and the July 2026 assessment rates it the country's only improvement. But state relief stops at the federal border, federal facilities and federal custody. No criminalisation of trans identity, plus functioning national hate-crime and employment protections, keeps this out of the high-risk bands; the universal federal exposures and custodial harm keep it out of reduced risk. Traveller with a minor adds federal care-hostility and school facility exposure against state-level care protection.
